biomarkers.name: Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Two pathways: MCPyV+ (integrated virus, lower TMB, often better prognosis) vs MCPyV- (UV-signature, very high TMB). Both are immunotherapy-responsive

biomarkers.name: Chromogranin A, synaptophysin, INSM1, CK20 (perinuclear dot)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic panel — CK20 perinuclear dot pattern is characteristic

biomarkers.name: PD-L1
biomarkers.clinical_use: PD-L1 expression is not required for use of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Avelumab is approved for metastatic MCC (JAVELIN Merkel 200); pembrolizumab and nivolumab also show activity. Responses occur in both MCPyV+ and MCPyV- disease

biomarkers.name: Antibody titre to MCPyV oncoproteins
biomarkers.prevalence: Present in a subset of patients with MCPyV+ MCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: MCPyV oncoprotein antibody testing (eg, AMERK at some centres) can help recurrence surveillance in seropositive MCC

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.prevalence: Very high in MCPyV-; low in MCPyV+
biomarkers.clinical_use: Primarily biologic/pathogenetic characterization rather than a validated treatment-selection biomarker in MCC; both MCPyV- and MCPyV+ disease can respond to immunotherapy

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small round blue cell tumour in dermis with neuroendocrine morphology (salt-and-pepper chromatin, high mitotic and apoptotic index)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Both viral and UV subtypes are immunotherapy-responsive but for different reasons — viral antigenicity in MCPyV+ disease and high UV-induced mutational/neoantigen burden in MCPyV- disease
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Dermal infiltrate; often ulceration; characteristic CK20 perinuclear dot pattern

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Uncertain — Merkel cells (mechanoreceptor cells) proposed but not proven; experimental evidence has also supported epithelial progenitors/keratinocytic lineage or dermal fibroblast origin depending on subtype/model
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Ectodermal epithelial/neuroendocrine differentiation is generally favored for Merkel cells; a neural crest origin for normal Merkel cells has also been proposed historically
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Neuroendocrine differentiation (synaptophysin+, chromogranin+, CK20+ with characteristic perinuclear dot pattern) with high proliferation and small round blue cell morphology
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Two distinct pathogenic pathways with different antigen profiles: MCPyV+ (viral, integrated Merkel cell polyomavirus with truncated large T antigen) and MCPyV- (UV-driven, high TMB)
